text:
Carmen: Heads-up  unusual behavior in us-west-2 rack-7. Dedicated pools approaching 98% allocation and we're seeing noisy-host symptoms (nvlink tx spikes + NIC bursts) causing short-chat P95s to jump ~140ms.
Diego: yikes. Which pools are hitting 98%? dedicated-small-slices?
Carmen: yes, dedicated-small and a few fractional reservations. When the allocator evicts tenants from the noisy hosts they spill into shared pools and we get cascading tail effects.
Nora: do we have cost telemetry on spillovers? spilling to shared increases token-cost per request and also increases infra churn.
Lee: I pulled the cost dashboard: spillovers increased GPU slot-hours by ~12% last 6h for that region; estimated $$ impact ~3.2k/day if sustained.
Carmen: Ops priority: stop the oscillation. Proposed immediate steps: 1) short-term: throttle best-effort batch jobs on the affected hosts, 2) enable a 2-minute cohort backoff so tenants evicted from a rack don't get requeued there, 3) prefer warm-pool routing for high-throughput tenants while the noisy host drains.
Diego: +1. Warm-pool preference will reduce stateful warmups and lower requeue churn. How invasive is the routing flag?
Nora: allocator supports a canary flip. We can patch a configmap to set prefer_warm_canary to 0.1 (10%) and monitor. If healthy bump to 50%.
Lee: sample command to canary the warm preference:
```
kubectl patch configmap allocator-policy -n fleet --type merge -p '{"data":{"prefer_warm_canary":"0.10"}}'
```
Carmen: also add metric panels for "requeue_cohort_backoff_count", "egress_spike_detected", and "dedicated_spillover_rate" to the dedicated preemptions dashboard.
Diego: will add them. Suggest we tag tenants that are high-state with "sticky=true" to avoid moving them while we debug.
Nora: long-term we should compare two paths: (A) invest in host-level IO QoS (NIC shaping + PCIe scheduling) vs (B) create small ephemeral carveouts for high-SLA tenants to eliminate noisy-neighbor risk. Path A reduces system complexity but costly infra work; path B increases reserved unit cost but simpler to operate. We should run a 1-week cost/latency sim.
Lee: I can run sim using last 30 days of allocation traces. Quick estimate: carving 5% capacity for high-SLA tenants reduces tail by ~20% but increases committed spend by ~7%.
Carmen: for now, enact the short-term mitigations. Diego, throttle commands?
Diego: running eBPF pacer on rack-7 for best-effort cgroup at 45% egress now.
ops-bot: eBPF pacer deployed to 6 hosts in us-west-2 rack-7 (tag: incident-3409876543).
Carmen: patching allocator canary to 10% now.
Diego: applying patch:
```
kubectl patch configmap allocator-policy -n fleet --type merge -p '{"data":{"prefer_warm_canary":"0.10","cohort_backoff_s":"120"}}'
```
ops-bot: Allocator configmap patched (prefer_warm_canary=0.10, cohort_backoff_s=120).
Nora: monitoring: nvlink peaks down ~28% after 90s, nic_tx bursts reduced. requeue_same_rack_count down ~45% in first 10m. P95 improved ~85ms.
Lee: cost telemetry: immediate churn-related slot-hours dropping; projection for next 24h down ~5% if trend holds.
Carmen: good. If canary stays green for 20m, increase prefer_warm_canary to 0.5 and keep cohort_backoff at 120s.
Diego: agreed. Also opening ticket INF-5110 to evaluate host IO QoS and INF-5111 to model carveout economics for high-SLA tenants.
Nora: small note: ensure we tag warm-pool allocations in billing so we can attribute any spend changes to canary.
Carmen: will follow up. Thanks team. If anyone sees tenant error-rate or timeouts > 0.5% revert immediately.
ops-bot: Incident annotation recorded by Diego at 3409876589 (incident-3409876543).
Lee: leaving a short runbook note in INF-5110 with the immediate mitigation steps and commands.
Carmen: thanks all. I'll post a summary to the incident board after the 30m window. :white_check_mark:
